overview: This study note examines the reasons why Israel was rejected, the remedy for that rejection, and the resulting consequences. It explores the causes of Israel's rejection, the necessary steps for belief, and the implications for God's relationship with His people.

topics.title: Reasons for Rejection
topics.summary: Israel was rejected due to several factors, including not feeling the need for salvation, being zealous for God by making their own traditions, being proud and self-righteous, and misunderstanding their law.
key_points: Did not feel the need for salvation; thought they were fine and could save themselves.
Were zealous for God but made their own traditions and worshipped them.
Were proud and self-righteous, refusing to listen and learn.
Misunderstood their own law; the law leads the sinner to the savior and must be obeyed in the heart.

topics.title: Remedy for Rejection
topics.summary: The remedy for rejection involves a missionary program, the interchangeability of believing and obeying, and the necessity of hearing before believing.
key_points: To believe one must first hear.

topics.title: Results of Rejection
topics.summary: The rejection of Israel resulted in Israel being guilty, the message being shared with Gentiles, and God still yearning for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty, even though Israel DID hear.
The message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel's rejection.
God still yearns for His people.
